chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Ghaffar al-Harithi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who left Mina intending to go to the House (Kaaba) before the middle of the night, and thus spent the dawn in Mecca. He said: 'It is not valid for him until he gives it as charity (sadaqah) or sheds blood (dams). But if he left Mina after the middle of the night, nothing will harm him.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House (Kaaba), the focal point of Islamic prayer and pilgrimage.
key_terms.صَدَقَةً: Charity, often used as a form of ransom (fidya) in Hajj.
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city containing the Kaaba.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Dhu al-Hijjah.
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: The middle of the night, a specific temporal marker in Hajj rituals.
key_terms.يُهْرِقَ دَمًا: Sheds blood, referring to the sacrifice of an animal (dams).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who leaves Mina before Fajr to perform Tawaf in Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani clarifies the temporal boundary for the validity of the Mina stay, distinguishing between early departure which incurs a penalty (sadaqah or dam) and late departure which is exempt. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the intention (niyyah) and the specific timeframe of 'middle of the night' as the cutoff for the ritual obligation, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the spirit of the Hajj rites without undue hardship.
